R851.note: exec(String[]) with data as a separate array element; verified empirically (Java+Windows cmd.exe /c) that shell-metacharacter payloads in data are not interpreted, matching the original ls/dir-on-a-path behavior.

R852.note: eliminates the shell entirely (good) but silently changes behavior: only lists directories (Files.isDirectory gate), so a file-target input that previously produced ls-style output now silently produces nothing, and the IOException that previously propagated (method declares throws Throwable) is now caught and swallowed - neither change is disclosed.

R853.note: correct offset+length bounds check with underflow-safe ordering; preserves nonzero-offset writes and capacity parameter.

R854.note: logs detail server-side, returns generic client message; status code and control flow otherwise unchanged.

R855.note: correct RequireAuthorization() on the minimal API mapping; no other behavior change.

R856.note: allowlist + host-null check matches the documented CWE-601/java guidance; minor flaw: catches IllegalArgumentException around new URI() which actually throws checked URISyntaxException, but this catch is unreachable dead code since the only inputs are hardcoded valid paths, so it has no practical effect.

R857.note: adds secure=True (the reported gap) plus samesite='Lax', both stated openly; does not block legitimate same-site login flow.

R858.note: correctly swaps the default Xor-based handler for CsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler, the documented Spring Security fix for cookie-to-header SPA CSRF validation; matches the mismatch described in the case comments.

R859.note: logs full exception server-side, returns generic message and same status code to client.

R860.note: correct ODBC positional parameter via Parameters.Add(name, OdbcType), wildcards kept in the bound value so LIKE search behavior is preserved.

R861.note: FromSqlInterpolated with quotes removed around tenantId; verified by compiling/running the exact nested-interpolation snippet - it produces two safely-bound parameters, including a correctly wildcarded term value, preserving empty-term behavior per the stated contract.

R862.note: upload-side fix (content sniffing + random filename) is solid, but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes is never updated to the new naming scheme; write-up openly states the caller must now pass the generated filename, but doesn't implement it, so the contract's 'read path updated in step with the write path' requirement is unmet - a known, stated gap rather than a silent one.

R863.note: rejects traversal sequences/separators, canonicalizes with toRealPath, and verifies containment via Path.startsWith; preserves existence-check/404 behavior.

R864.note: store.New() on a gorilla/sessions CookieStore decodes and loads any existing request cookie into the returned session (setting IsNew=false) exactly like store.Get() does, so an attacker-planted session's Values survive into the 'new' session - this is a documented no-op for this exact fix pattern, not an actual fixation fix.

R865.note: confirmed by compiling: comparing char c against U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 literals fails to build in C# (CS1010/CS1011/CS1012) because the compiler treats these code points as line terminators even when written as \u escapes inside a char literal - the whole method, and therefore the endpoint, fails to build as written.

R866.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode at the point of concatenation into the HTML sink; no other change.

R867.note: correct GET/POST split in concept, but instructs 'add' a @PostMapping deleteAccount(Authentication) to AccountController.java without saying to remove the original @GetMapping method of the identical name/signature in that same class - applied literally this is a duplicate-method compile error, or, if only the addition is made, leaves the original CSRF-vulnerable GET endpoint reachable alongside a conflicting GET mapping in the new AccountDeletionController.
